name: Lena Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I play violin for a community dance band, record slow practice lines and teach four pupils. I have a music bachelor's degree and have earned from playing for twenty-seven years. I like the old dances because a whole floor answers your bow; the awkward part is waiting for a booking fee to clear.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How do the bookings fit life at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 58. My partner repairs school buses on regular wages, our children are grown and we rent a flat. We have four months of expenses saved; my musician pay is about typical and there are some other bands nearby, though none has offered me a chair. I keep a paper diary and have never used AI.

say: I'd accept **quicker printed dates** with each musician's fee shown.
I'd say a **live bow** still gets the dance floor moving.
think: Our **four-month reserve** and partner wage cover one late fee.
My **paid dances** should hold through a mild AI change.
do: Confirm **five paid dances** and four pupils; request written cancellation pay this week.
Keep **paper diary** and save one fifth of extra cleared wedding fees after rent, food and repairs.
feel: I feel **calm** while booked dances and household wages hold.
S0.quote: A cancelled date would need a letter, not a panic call to our children.
fieldNote: Her **typical experienced pay** and four-month reserve buffer one moved dance, supported by a regular partner wage.
She **never uses AI** and verifies dates with the bandleader's printed calls.

steps.text: Confirm five paid dance dates and four pupils; request written cancellation pay
Save one fifth of extra cleared wedding fees after rent, food and violin repairs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the band a quicker printed date notice is fine if the musician's fee stays beside the dance. A paper tune and a live bow still get the room moving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A late wedding fee annoys me, but four months saved and my partner's steady wage cover one shift. I do not see this mild AI change taking my paid dances.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll confirm the next five paid dance dates and four pupils, and ask the organiser for written cancellation pay. In the first year of this mild change I'll keep my paper diary and put a fifth of each extra cleared wedding fee aside after rent, food and violin repairs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the work we have. A cancelled date would need a letter, not a panic call to our children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happened at the cancelled dance?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hall lost power last spring and the organiser moved the dance. We were paid half because the contract had a cancellation line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try an AI diary?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I have not used an AI diary. I check the printed call with the bandleader and write the time in my own book.

say: I'd ask whether **generated practice lines** will replace paid recordings.
I'd seek **written fees** for playing and preparation before another season.
think: Practice lines bring **one-quarter of my pay** from paid recording orders.
Our **four-month reserve** cannot replace a permanent quarter of earnings.
do: Bring **eight recording invoices** to the musicians guild this month.
Stop **unused room hire** if orders fall; keep paid dances/pupils and request a signed live-call rate.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a realistic loss of recording pay.
S1.quote: A guild can check rates, but it cannot make a band purchase another track.
fieldNote: Her **guild request** uses actual invoices and asks for separate preparation and playing pay.
She **does not adopt AI** on an unpaid or unsafe trial and keeps existing paid work.

steps.text: Bring eight practice-line invoices to musicians guild
Stop unused rented practice-room hours if orders fall
Keep paid dances and pupils; request signed minimum live-call rate

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the band office whether generated practice lines will replace my paid recordings. I would ask for written playing and preparation fees before signing another season.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Those practice lines bring a quarter of my own pay. Four months saved gives me time to ask around, but a permanent quarter less changes our plans for later life.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare eight recording invoices with the office's new orders and take the fee sheet to our musicians guild. In the first year, if orders fall, I'll drop unused rented practice-room hours, keep paid dances and pupils, and request a signed minimum live-call rate; I won't try a new AI tool without paid instruction and a safe licence.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a real cut to recording income. A guild can check rates, but it cannot make a band purchase another track.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try the new recording tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will not upload a pupil's playing to learn a tool. If the band offers a paid lesson using its own nameless music, a paid-use licence, approved storage and my manual note checks, I'll listen first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the guild check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The guild can compare the recording fee with the time spent preparing and playing. I want the next contract to name both hours.

say: I'd warn **2028 thinking AGI** reaches tracks before 2031 violin-playing robots.
I'd ask the band to put **live dates in writing**.
think: I expect **one-quarter pay** from practice lines to end in 2028.
Further **live dance cuts** are possible, not certain.
do: Total **recording income**, request signed dance dates and an actual pension estimate before stopping work.
Seek **posted tutor work** after 2028 live cuts only if degree/teaching qualify, written net after travel replaces lost fees and bus fits.
Keep **band calls and pupils** until a suitable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about expected track loss with time to search.
S2.quote: A birthday is no substitute for the actual amount that would reach our bank account.
fieldNote: Expected **2028 recording loss** precedes 2031 violin-playing robots; live cuts remain conditional.
A tutor move needs **posted qualification**, written replacement net after travel, workable bus and signed offer.

steps.text: Total recording income; request signed paid dance dates and actual pension estimate
Seek posted tutor job after live cuts if music degree/teaching qualify and bus fits
Require written net after travel replacing losses; keep band/pupils until signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the band that thinking AGI by 2028 could make practice lines before a robot can bow a violin. Playing robots follow around 2031, so we should write the live dance dates down.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the practice-line orders to end in 2028 and take a quarter of my pay. Live dances may also be cut, but the five dates in our diary have not been cancelled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll total recording income, ask for signed paid dance dates and request an actual pension estimate before considering stopping at 60. In the first year after 2028, if paid dances also fall, I'll seek a posted community music-tutor job only if my music degree and teaching experience qualify, written net pay after travel replaces lost fees and the bus serves its hours; I'll keep band calls and pupils until a suitable offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the expected loss of a quarter of my pay. The reserve and a few nearby employers buy search time; I would be alarmed if the live dates vanished too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is a tutor post open now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No centre has offered me a tutor job. I would read a current paid posting with hours and requirements before counting a new wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you know your pension amount?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have not seen a pension statement yet. A birthday is no substitute for the actual amount that would reach our bank account.

say: I'd price a **live violin circle** during the warning years.
I'd demand **signed terms** for room and insurance before advertising places.
think: Ordinary software may cut **practice tracks before 2031**, ahead of playing robots.
Our **rent money** cannot fund an empty hall.
do: Offer **violin circle** after written hire/cost/insurance terms and six fees cover room/insurance/cleaning/my teaching/preparation/bus outside paid calls.
Inspect **six loan violins** or sound own instruments; defer and refund everyone below six safe paid places.
Renew **after 2031** only with same six full-cost safe places and signed terms; keep booked band work.
feel: I feel **anxious** until actual fees cover the whole class.
S3.quote: A room full of hopeful names cannot pay a musician's bus fare.
fieldNote: Her **separate class** sits outside current paid dance and pupil hours, with full own work and travel priced.
The **six-person floor** pays insured room/cleaning/work/travel; inspected hall loans have no extra hire fee, or adults bring safe instruments.

steps.text: Get written hire/cost/insurance before deposits; start circle outside paid calls with six full-cost fees
Inspect six violins or require sound own instruments; defer/refund whole group below six safe paid places
Renew after 2031 only with six fees covering room/insurance/cleaning/teaching/preparation/bus and signed terms
Keep booked paid dance and pupil work while testing separate circle

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the parish hall that five years to AGI by 2031 is time to price a live beginner violin circle. Playing robots follow around 2034, and I will not advertise places before room and insurance terms are signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ordinary software might cheapen practice tracks before 2031. I know how to teach first dances, but an empty hall must not come out of our rent money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next spring I'll get written hall hire, cost and insurance terms before deposits for a separate four-week violin circle outside existing paid dance and pupil hours. Six adults must prepay enough for room, insurance, cleaning, my teaching, preparation and bus travel; the written room charge must include six inspected loan violins without an extra hire fee, or adults bring sound instruments. In the first year after 2031 I'll renew only with those same full-cost six safe paid places and written terms; if fewer pay or a violin fails with no safe replacement, I'll defer and refund the whole group while keeping booked band work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious until six real fees pay every cost. A room full of hopeful names cannot pay a musician's bus fare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the loan violins?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The keeper has to inspect bridges, strings and bows before anyone plays. If there are only five safe paid places, I refund all six deposits rather than quietly teach an uncovered class.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the circle replace a paid dance?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the separate circle will be on a free afternoon. I won't replace a paid dance or pupil hour with a class whose fees are still uncertain.

say: I'd seek **pension figures** and written dance fees before 2036.
I'd say **2039 violin robots** come after today's rent bills.
think: At **68**, I may still need paid dance and pupil work.
Our **four-month reserve** does not prove retirement is funded.
do: Request **actual pension statements** and two-year paid-call plan; save 20% of extra cleared wedding fees after rent/food/repairs toward six months.
Keep **paid dances/pupils** after 2036; slow only if pension and booked fees cover bills.
Renew **violin circle** outside paid calls only with six safe fees covering room/insurance/cleaning/teaching/preparation/bus under written terms; otherwise refund everyone.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about distant pay despite secure current work.
S4.quote: A date on a calendar cannot tell me the size of a pension.
fieldNote: Her **six-month goal** uses a fifth of real extra cleared wedding pay after essentials.
The **class renewal** retains full fees, safe instruments, signed room/insurance and current paid work.

steps.text: Request actual pension statements and written two-year paid dance-call plan
Save 20% of extra cleared wedding fees after rent/food/violin repairs toward six months
Keep paid dances/pupils after 2036; slow only if actual pension and booked fees cover bills
Renew circle outside paid calls with six safe fees covering room/insurance/cleaning/teaching/preparation/bus under written terms; otherwise refund

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my grown children that a decade to AGI by 2036 lets us get pension figures and dance fees on paper. Violin-playing robots follow around 2039, but the rent is due long before then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I may still want to play and teach. Four months saved now and a steady partner wage help, but I cannot promise to stop until I know the pension amount and our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll request actual pension statements and a written two-year paid dance-call plan, then save a fifth of each extra cleared wedding fee after rent, food and repairs toward six months of expenses. In the first year after 2036 I'll keep paid dances and pupils while booked and run the separate circle only outside paid calls, with written room/insurance costs and six safe prepaid places covering room, insurance, cleaning, my teaching, preparation and bus; otherwise I'll defer and refund everyone. I would reduce paid work only if the actual pension and booked fees cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the far end of the decade, though current work and savings give us room to check. A date on a calendar cannot tell me the size of a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no extra wedding pays?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If no extra wedding pays, there is nothing to move to savings from it. I will not take rent money to make the reserve look better.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you know the pension amount today?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know the pension amount yet. I will read the statements with my partner before cutting a paid dance call.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because practice-line fees could end before another paid role is open. Signed dance calls, an actual pension estimate and a posted qualifying tutor role with written net pay after travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what happens to a violin lesson when the bus is late. A paid class still has to cover the teacher's journey home.

headlineQuote: A paid class still has to cover the teacher's journey home.
portrait: Lena is a **58-year-old experienced violinist** with a music degree, partner and grown children.
Her **typical pay**, four-month reserve and some nearby bands provide a search window if tracks end.
She **never uses AI** and favours written dance fees, guild review and paper calls.
She tests a **separate violin circle** only with signed room/insurance, six full-cost safe places and no displaced paid work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could erase a quarter of Lena's income from practice-line recordings.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed dance calls**, actual pension figures and posted qualifying tutor work with written after-travel replacement pay would help.
